meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: with a past-tense verb: я бы подумал = I would think
wishes: купили бы = we could have bought

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'eastern', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: Today we are saving Far Eastern leopards.
And also our Far Eastern rat snake.

meanings.note: Used for women too. From Latin 'director' (one who guides or manages, from 'dirigere', to direct).
Used for women too. From Latin 'director' (one who guides or manages, from 'dirigere', to direct).

examples.trans: I want to talk to the director.

examples.text: Я один раз позвонила как директор и отменила контрольную.
examples.trans: Once I phoned pretending to be the headmistress and cancelled a test.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to reach, arrive at by vehicle
meanings.note: Intransitive perfective verb. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ехать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to reach, arrive', paired with 'доезжать'.

examples.trans: They reached the station on time.
I simply want to arrive faster.

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.
Ещё больше = even more. Core Russian adv meaning 'more; still; yet' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Animate neuter noun. Common neuter noun meaning 'animal' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я добрый человек, я люблю животных.
examples.trans: I am a kind person, I love animals.

заболеть.gloss: to fall ill, to get sick

meanings.en: to fall ill, to come down with an illness
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'болеть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fall ill, to get sick', paired with 'болеть'.

examples.text: Вчера он заболел и остался дома.
examples.trans: Yesterday he fell ill and stayed at home.

examples.text: А у меня учительница по математике заболела.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'kitchen', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: У вас на кухне живая змея!
examples.trans: There is a live snake in your kitchen!
He planted a live snake on us!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'zoo' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Where did I just walk in, a zoo?

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый зоопарк.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new zoo.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Diminutive of кот. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'kitten; honey, baby' in everyday Russian.
Affectionate pet name for a man. Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'kitten; honey, baby' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нет, котик, я всё понимаю. Но я не буду воровать собаку.
examples.trans: No, kitten, I understand everything. But I'm not going to steal a dog.

examples.text: У многих из вас появились сомнения. Хочу сказать вам.
examples.trans: Many of you have begun to have doubts. I want to tell you.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('sea / marine').

examples.trans: Right here is our fur seal.
And where is our fur seal?

examples.text: Сегодня у нас морской котик и норка.
examples.trans: Today we have a fur seal and a mink.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'flies' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They are simply dropping like flies.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть муха.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always flies.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

Usually singular collective. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'equipment, machinery' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это договор на покупку строительного оборудования.
examples.trans: This is a contract for the purchase of construction equipment.

examples.trans: And what equipment do I have?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'держать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to support, to back', paired with 'поддерживать'.

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'кинуться'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to money'.

examples.text: Так что нам всем надо скинуться.
examples.trans: So we all need to chip in money.
We chipped in here as a whole team.

meanings.note: Intransitive, reflexive. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ломаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break down, get broken', paired with 'ломаться'.

examples.trans: Yesterday the washing machine broke down.

meanings.note: К сожалению = unfortunately. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'regret, pity' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: Unfortunately, you are not my type.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives
Я считаю, что... = I think that. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to count; to think, to consider', paired with 'посчитать'.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Direction. Core Russian adv meaning 'here (to this place)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

Core Russian part meaning 'even if, at least (with бы); although' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.
